claims.summary: CLAUDE.md and scoped rules provide first-party persistent instructions. They guide model behavior; they are not an enforcement boundary.
The reviewed project-instruction source does not define a complete cloud-surface loading contract.
AGENTS.md is the documented repository instruction contract, with hierarchical scope for more specific directories.
Copilot supports repository-wide, path-specific, and agent instruction files; exact file support varies by product surface.
Claude Code documents command, prompt, agent, HTTP, and MCP-tool hooks across lifecycle events and settings scopes.
Codex exposes first-party local lifecycle hooks. OpenAI explicitly describes hooks as guardrails, not complete policy enforcement.
The reviewed official hooks reference documents the local Codex hook boundary, not an equivalent cloud hook runtime.
Copilot documents lifecycle hooks and decision control, but hook timeouts fail open; use them as automation and guardrails, not a universal hard-policy boundary.
Claude Code implements Agent Skills with progressive disclosure, manual or model invocation, scripts, resources, and product-specific controls.
Codex documents reusable skills as the first-party packaging mechanism for repeatable workflows and supporting resources.
Copilot documents Agent Skills for specialized instructions, scripts, and resources, with product-specific discovery and precedence.
Claude Code supports built-in and custom subagents with isolated context, tool and model controls, and nested delegation.
Codex enables built-in and custom subagents by default and surfaces their parallel work as coordinator-managed threads.
Copilot documents custom agents with isolated context and role-specific tools, used as subagents by the primary agent.
Agent teams provide independent teammate sessions, a shared task list, mailboxes, and peer messaging, but Anthropic still labels the feature experimental.
Codex runs parallel specialized subagents and collects results through the main coordinator. The reviewed docs do not describe a peer mailbox or shared task-ledger topology.
Copilot CLI Fleet decomposes work across parallel subagents and documents sibling-agent discovery and messaging.
Claude Code provides first-party MCP configuration and connection management for external tools and data sources.
Codex documents first-party MCP client configuration for extending local agent tool and context access.
Copilot CLI provides first-party MCP server configuration and management.
Copilot cloud agent supports MCP tools, but the documented surface excludes resources, prompts, and remote OAuth.
Claude Code provides built-in commands and invocable custom workflows; skills are now the recommended packaging model for multi-step commands.
Codex CLI documents an interactive slash-command surface, while repeatable custom workflows are packaged as skills.
Copilot CLI provides built-in slash commands plus command files as a simplified, lower-priority alternative to skills.
Claude Code documents layered settings, permissions, managed policy, environment controls, and configuration precedence.
Codex exposes a first-party configuration file and layered controls for models, sandboxing, approvals, and extensions.
Copilot CLI provides personal settings, permissions, provider, extension, and agent customization controls.
Claude Code combines human-authored CLAUDE.md context with machine-authored, repository-scoped local auto memory.
Local Codex clients use a local memory store and per-chat controls; required team rules still belong in AGENTS.md or checked-in documentation.
ChatGPT and hosted work use separate account or workspace memory behavior rather than the local Codex memory store and controls.
Copilot CLI documents a memory tool and explicit memory enablement controls for prompt-mode sessions.
The reviewed CLI source is insufficient to assert one shared memory contract across Copilot's editor, web, and cloud surfaces.
The reviewed hook reference is insufficient to assert the same lifecycle contract on Claude Code's hosted surface.
The reviewed skills reference is insufficient to classify hosted discovery and invocation as equivalent to local clients.
The reviewed subagent reference does not establish a complete hosted-surface contract equivalent to local clients.
The reviewed experimental agent-teams reference does not establish equivalent IDE and hosted coordination behavior.
The reviewed MCP source does not define a complete hosted capability and authentication matrix.
The reviewed command reference is terminal-centered and does not establish identical IDE or hosted command availability.
The reviewed settings source is insufficient to classify the hosted configuration and managed-policy surface as equivalent.
Claude's documented local auto-memory store is machine-local; the reviewed source does not establish an equivalent hosted store.
The reviewed AGENTS.md source does not establish one general web-surface loading contract outside the named Codex clients and cloud workflows.
The reviewed hook reference does not establish a browser-hosted hook runtime.
The reviewed build-skills source is insufficient to classify skill discovery and execution across web and cloud as equivalent to local clients.
Hosted subagent workflows are documented, but availability and controls differ from configurable local Codex agents.
Hosted parallel subagents are documented as coordinator-managed workflows; the source does not describe a peer team with shared task state.
The reviewed MCP source is insufficient to assert one hosted capability, transport, and authentication contract.
The reviewed slash-command source is CLI-specific and does not establish identical commands on IDE, web, or cloud surfaces.
The reviewed config-file source does not establish an equivalent hosted configuration contract.
GitHub documents instruction support on selected web experiences, but supported file types and behavior vary by feature.
The reviewed hooks source does not establish the same event and decision contract for general IDE and web interactions.
The reviewed CLI sources are insufficient to classify skill discovery and invocation on IDE and web surfaces.
The reviewed CLI customization sources do not establish one equivalent custom-agent contract for IDE and web surfaces.
Fleet is documented for Copilot CLI; the reviewed sources do not establish the same team topology on IDE, web, or cloud surfaces.
The reviewed CLI and cloud sources are insufficient to classify the remaining IDE and web MCP surfaces as equivalent.
The reviewed command reference is CLI-specific and does not establish identical commands elsewhere in the Copilot family.
The reviewed CLI settings source is insufficient to define one equivalent configuration contract across the wider Copilot family.
